title: Interactive trace sandbox: span annotation lanes and correlation folding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Engineers using Redwood Console need a faster way to investigate tail latency and token-level cost spikes across requests. Existing trace drilldowns are powerful but require multiple panels and manual correlation across lists and timelines. Scope: design an interactive 'trace sandbox' panel that surfaces a horizontally scrollable timeline with per-span annotation lanes, atomic span actions (pin, annotate, hide), correlation-id folding, and an integrated cost-per-span micro-report. The sandbox is intended as a lightweight, copyable workspace for deep dives and bug bisection, not a full replay tool. Goals: 1) let users quickly fold/unfold related spans by correlation ID; 2) add and persist lightweight annotations tied to specific spans and time ranges; 3) expose per-span token-cost estimates and highlight outliers; 4) support copyable segment links and exportable snippet of spans for postmortems. Constraints: must reuse existing trace data model (no new backend indexes), maintain console performance targets (render <100ms for 200-span traces), and keep accessibility keyboard flows for lane actions.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas shows timeline with span lanes and lane-level compact annotations
Users can fold all spans with the same correlation ID via one-click and revert
Span annotations are persisted per-user and visible on reload for the same trace
Per-span cost micro-report displays token count, estimated GPU-ms, and a hint color for high-cost spans
Lane actions (pin/annotate/hide) are keyboard accessible and present in the context menu
Sharing: ‘Copy segment link’ generates a stable URL with time-range and pinned spans

2025-03-07 — Engineering sync: ENG pointed to a safe-first approach — implement client-side fold and annotation store in user preferences (no new server writes yet).
2025-03-11 — Design review: accessibility pass completed; keyboard flows and ARIA labels added to annotations and fold controls.
decisions: Persist annotations in user-scoped metadata (client will POST to /user/annotations) to avoid trace schema changes
Implement correlation folding purely client-side using existing span.parent_id and correlation_id tags
Cost estimates derived from existing token counts and model profile lookup; show as heuristic only
Ship as an opt-in beta behind feature flag console.tracing.sandbox
